quizzes.title: National Song and National Anthem: Status and Protection
quizzes.passage:
India recognises two songs in connection with its national identity: the National Anthem, Jana Gana Mana, and the National Song, Vande Mataram. The two songs do not hold identical positions. Jana Gana Mana is the National Anthem. Vande Mataram was given the status of National Song after independence.

Respect for national symbols is also linked to the duties of citizens. The fundamental duties in the Constitution ask every citizen to respect the National Flag and the National Anthem. Parliamentary practice gives the anthem a ceremonial role as well, because sittings of Parliament begin with it.

Existing legislation already protects the National Flag and the Constitution from intentional insult or disrespect, and acts such as burning, defacing or desecrating the flag are covered. The anthem also receives statutory protection, which makes it an offence to intentionally prevent its singing or to disturb an assembly during its rendition.

A 2026 amendment proposal would extend this framework to Vande Mataram. Intentionally insulting the song, or obstructing its singing, would become punishable, placing it within the same legal framework that protects the anthem. The stated objective is to give Vande Mataram statutory protection similar to the protection the anthem currently has. The anthem's existing protection is therefore the model for the proposed change, which would apply the same offences to a second national symbol.

questions.q: On what date did Dr. Rajendra Prasad declare Vande Mataram the National Song of India?
questions.explanation: Vande Mataram was declared the National Song on 24 January 1950, the same day Jana Gana Mana was adopted as the anthem.

questions.q: Under which Article of the Constitution are the fundamental duties to respect the National Flag and National Anthem listed?
questions.explanation: Article 51A(a) asks citizens to respect the National Flag and the National Anthem.

questions.q: Which existing statute already protects the National Anthem from intentional disruption?
options: Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971
questions.explanation: The Prevention of Insults to National Honour Act, 1971 already protects the anthem, and the 2026 Bill seeks similar protection for Vande Mataram.

questions.q:
Read the assertion and reason and choose the correct option.
Assertion (A): The Constitution of India explicitly recognises a National Song.
Reason (R): Vande Mataram was given the status of National Song after independence.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The Constitution does not explicitly recognise a National Song, but Vande Mataram was given that status after independence.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Vande Mataram   ->   A. Written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay
II. Jana Gana Mana   ->   B. Composed by Rabindranath Tagore
III. First public use on 7 August 1905   ->   C. Town Hall, Calcutta
IV. Goddess imagery in Vande Mataram   ->   D. Goddess Durga
questions.explanation: Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay wrote Vande Mataram, Tagore composed Jana Gana Mana, and the song's imagery is of Goddess Durga.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the national songs:
I. The entire text of Jana Gana Mana has official recognition.
II. Parliamentary sittings are closed sine die with Vande Mataram.
III. Vande Mataram is at present protected under the 1971 Act.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II are correct, while the 1971 Act does not yet cover Vande Mataram.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the two songs:
I. Vande Mataram was to be honoured equally with the National Anthem.
II. Parliamentary sittings are closed sine die with the National Anthem.
III. Vande Mataram was composed by Rabindranath Tagore.
How many of the above statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, since sittings close with Vande Mataram and the song was written by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.

quizzes.title: Anthem, Song and the Constitution
quizzes.passage:
India's two national songs have different legal and symbolic positions. Jana Gana Mana is the National Anthem and carries full official recognition as a national symbol. Vande Mataram is the National Song, a status it was given after independence, although the Constitution does not explicitly provide for a national song at all.

Respect for national symbols is part of civic life. The fundamental duties ask citizens to respect the National Flag and the National Anthem, and both the flag and the anthem are protected by law from insult. Parliament reflects the same respect in its own practice, since its sittings are opened with the anthem.

Vande Mataram has a long history in public life. It appeared in the Bengali novel Anandamath and was composed as a patriotic response to a British promotion of a song. The song praises Mother India through an image of a goddess.

A 2026 amendment proposal would extend legal protection to Vande Mataram. Under the proposal, intentionally insulting the song or preventing its singing would become punishable. The stated aim is to give the song statutory protection comparable to what the anthem already enjoys, bringing the national song into the same legal framework as the flag and the anthem.

questions.q: On what date was Jana Gana Mana adopted as the National Anthem? (give the full date)
questions.explanation: Jana Gana Mana was adopted as the National Anthem on 24 January 1950, with the entire anthem officially recognised.

questions.q: Under which Article of the Constitution are the fundamental duties to respect the National Flag and National Anthem listed? (give the article number with its letter)
questions.explanation: Article 51A(a) requires citizens to respect the National Flag and National Anthem.

questions.q: Who declared Vande Mataram as the National Song of India? (give the full name)
questions.explanation: Dr. Rajendra Prasad made the declaration on 24 January 1950.

questions.q: Who composed the tune of Jana Gana Mana? (give the name)
questions.explanation: Jana Gana Mana was written and composed by Rabindranath Tagore.

questions.q: In which year was Jana Gana Mana composed? (give the year)
questions.explanation: Jana Gana Mana was composed in 1911 and first sung the same year.

questions.q: Vande Mataram was composed as a patriotic response to the British promotion of which song? (give the song's name)
accept: God Save the King or Queen
questions.explanation: Vande Mataram was composed as a patriotic response to the British promotion of God Save the King/Queen.

questions.q: At which venue was Vande Mataram first publicly used on 7 August 1905? (give the venue)
questions.explanation: Vande Mataram's first public use on 7 August 1905 was at the Town Hall in Calcutta.
